Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Acme is excited to move into a hands-on POC. We'd like to schedule a series of 3 technical deep dives (prompt review, routing experiments, and load tests) that run as rotating windows so colleagues in US / EU / APAC can join at least one session in reasonable hours.

Proposed constraints from our side:
- Prefer 90-minute blocks
- Want both a brief architecture walk and 45–60 minutes for hands-on work (prompt tuning, routing rules, short load tests)
- We can commit product and infra engineers for the week of Nov 29–Dec 3, but need a firm schedule by Nov 15 to block travel and overlap windows.

Suggested rotating start times (examples):
- US-friendly: 08:00 PT / 16:00 CET / 00:00 JST
- EU-friendly: 11:00 PT / 19:00 CET / 03:00 JST
- APAC-friendly: 16:00 PT / 00:00 CET / 08:00 JST

I've attached our availability matrix (availability_matrix.xlsx) — small file. Can your team propose a rotation that maps to Redwood owners for each session (who will run prompt review, who owns routing/load tests)? Also, is Redwood able to provide a short test-plan CSV for the load tests so we can pre-populate metrics and thresholds?

Thanks,
Akiko
Product Program Manager
Acme Robotics

Hi Akiko — really appreciate the clear constraints and the matrix. I ran this by the Tech Enablement leads and here are two ways we can structure the three rotating deep dives:

Option A (role-aligned rotation):
- Session A: Prompt review + guided prompt workshop — owner: Lauren (developer experience)
- Session B: Routing & fallbacks + policy routing — owner: Karthik (runtime routing)
- Session C: Load tests & observability checklist — owner: Marcus (performance + infra)

Option B (time-aligned rotation):
- Each 90-min session follows the same agenda, but owners rotate so our experts are available in local hours. This is heavier on coordination but easier for your cross-team attendance.

Quick asks from our side:
- Confirm which of your engineers will lead the hands-on portion for routing/load tests (name + timezone).
- Do you want us to run short canary load ramps (5–10 min) during the sessions or do you prefer offline runs?

I created a quick Doodle-style poll / calendar-proposal: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abc123-def456 — please pick preferred rotation rows by Nov 10.

I'll draft an agenda and a lightweight load-test CSV and attach both once we converge.

Best,
